title: A cochain realization of the three prescribed support comparisons
statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field, A a finite commutative ring, T a separated finite-type k-scheme and i:C→T a closed immersion. Suppose etale and pro-etale support boundaries δe and δp satisfy supportBoundaryNormalization [def-pur-support-comparison-boundary-maps]. For every ordinary etale A-module sheaf F in degree zero, the two graded support localization rows admit short exact cochain models and a morphism of those models inducing precisely the three prescribed support, global-section and open-section comparison maps of [def-pur-support-comparison-boundary-maps]. The row identification respects all arrows, including the two specified snake boundaries; this is Nonempty(SupportComparisonSnakeModel …) [lem-pur-support-snake-model-naturality].

proof.text: Choose bounded-below termwise injective representatives I of K=F[0] and L of βD K, where β is the exact ordinary comparison inverse image. Bounded-below injective complexes are K-injective. Fullness of localization on maps into the K-injective target lifts the canonical derived identification Q(β I)→βD K to a chain map b:β I→L. Its composite with the chosen target identification is that canonical identification.

For each additive section functor G on the etale side and G′ on the pro-etale side, with its ordinary comparison ε:G→β G′, map ε termwise on I and compose with G′(b). Its homology map represents the normalized right-derived base-change map. To prove this, use the base-change factorization through the right-derived unit at the homotopy object of I; apply naturality of the target derived unit to b, use the equation defining b, and apply naturality of base change to QI≅K. Finally take homology and use naturality of homologyFunctorObjQIso. All coherence maps, including the identity-derived-functor and composite-functor isomorphisms, are kept in this calculation.

For both sites use the explicit kernel/restriction cochain rows supplied by the normalization assumptions. The canonical injectiveHomologyModelIso identifies the three terms with the graded support, global-section and open-section functors. Derived-natural-transformation compatibility gives the inclusion and restriction identities. The assumed boundary identity at QI and naturality of δ along the chosen model isomorphism give its identity at K.

Apply Step 2 to supported sections, ambient sections and open sections. The defining kernel-inclusion condition of supportComparisonUnit makes the first cochain square commute; ordinary adjunction-unit naturality with respect to restriction makes the second commute. Naturality of the pro-etale inclusion and restriction also commutes each with b. The three component formulas from Step 2 are exactly the maps recorded in SupportComparisonBoundaryMaps, so this is the required SupportComparisonSnakeModel.

theorem exists_supportComparison_injective_ladder
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    (T : Scheme.{u}) [T.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (T ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [QuasiCompact (T ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [IsSeparated (T ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    (C : Scheme.{u}) (i : C ⟶ T) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (δₑ : Sheaf.SupportSequenceBoundary T.smallEtaleTopology
      (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) (Etale.supportRestrictionArrow i) ⊤)
    (δₚ : Sheaf.SupportSequenceBoundary (Scheme.ProEt.topology T)
      (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) (ProEtale.supportRestrictionArrow i) ⊤)
    (hₑ : supportBoundaryNormalization T.smallEtaleTopology A
      (Etale.supportRestrictionArrow i) δₑ)
    (hₚ : supportBoundaryNormalization (Scheme.ProEt.topology T) A
      (ProEtale.supportRestrictionArrow i) δₚ)
    (F : Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) :
    Nonempty (SupportComparisonSnakeModel
      (supportBoundaryHomologyRow T.smallEtaleTopology A
        (Etale.supportRestrictionArrow i) δₑ
        ((DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor
          (Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) 0).obj F))
      (supportBoundaryHomologyRow (Scheme.ProEt.topology T) A
        (ProEtale.supportRestrictionArrow i) δₚ
        ((DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor
          (Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) 0 ⋙
          (ProEtale.comparisonUpperStar
            (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) T).mapDerivedCategoryPlus).obj F))
      (fun q ↦ (ProEtale.supportComparisonHypercohomology A i q).app
        ((DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor
          (Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) 0).obj F))
      (fun q ↦ (ProEtale.finiteComparisonGlobalHypercohomology T A q).app
        ((DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor
          (Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) 0).obj F))
      (fun q ↦ (ProEtale.finiteComparisonSectionHypercohomology T A
        (Scheme.Etale.mk i.openComplement.ι) q).app
        ((DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor
          (Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) 0).obj F)))
